provenance.title: COHOMOLOGICAL DONALDSON–THOMAS THEORY OF A
provenance.authors: QUIVER WITH POTENTIAL AND QUANTUM ENVELOPING

candidates.statement: The main conclusion of this paper is that the introduction of the cohomological Hall algebra structure associated to a quiver, a potential and a Serre subcategory $\mathcal{S}$ should be seen as a first step towards forging a connection between the theory of refined Donaldson--Thomas invariants and the theory of quantum enveloping algebras, and that the proof of the integrality conjecture is the motivic shadow of a Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the associated quantum enveloping algebra.

[]{#abvsrel label="abvsrel"} For the Donaldson--Thomas theory and cohomological Hall algebras associated to quivers, a vital role is always played by the grading by $\mathbb{N}^{Q_0}$, the semigroup of dimension vectors, which should be seen as a weight space decomposition in the language of Lie algebras and quantum groups.

To define this "appropriate sense", we must take some care over the signs in the symmetrizing morphism $$\textbf{sw}:\mathcal{F}\boxtimes_+ \mathcal{F}\rightarrow \mathcal{F}\boxtimes_+\mathcal{F}.$$ It was noted already in [@KS2] that the cohomological Hall algebra on the graded vector space ([\[baby\]](#baby){reference-type="ref" reference="baby"}), while not commutative, becomes commutative after twisting by a simple system of signs.
candidates.section_title: Main results for cohomological Hall algebras

candidates.statement: The categorification of this picture, then, should be a monoidal category, for which the monoidal product cannot be upgraded to a symmetric monoidal product, except on fixed subcategories indexed by the slope $\upmu$, for which we should define a symmetric monoidal product.
